recipes.name: Water Tribe Noodles inspired by The Legend of Korra
ingredients: 1 fish bones & carcass from white fish, such as tilapia or cod
2 , (one inch) long piece of ginger, sliced
3 green onions, cut into (three inch) pieces
instructions: In a medium mixing bowl, add fish bones, carcass, wine and salt. Using your hands, coat the fish bones in the wine and salt and allow to sit for 5-10 minutes. - 1 fish bones & carcass from white fish such as tilapia or cod - 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine - kosher salt to taste
While the fish is marinating, prepare the aromatics by slicing ginger and green onions. - 2 (one inch) long piece of ginger, sliced - 3 green onions cut into (three inch) pieces
In a wok or Dutch oven over medium high heat, add oil. Once shimmering, add ginger and scallions and stir to combine. - 1 tbsp neutral oil
Once the aromatics are fragrant, add fish bones and carcass with water to cover. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. - 1 ½ cups water

Cook for 30-45 minutes, skimming any scum that rises to the surface using a paper towel. Once the fish bones are softened, strain the stock through a fine mesh sieve. Set aside and cover. Refrigerate until ready to use. - For the Fish Stock
In a medium saucepan add water and bring to a boil. Then add spinach and cook for several minutes to allow it to wilt. - 1 ½ cups water - 3 cups spinach
Then transfer to a blender, reserving the liquid in a heat-proof bowl. Blend until paste-like consistency and the fibers are pulverized, then strain through a fine mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth.
In a mixing bowl, combine flour, salt, and kelp powder. Whisk until homogenous. - 2 cups all purpose flour - 1 tsp salt - 1 tsp spirulina/kelp powder
Then add all of the spinach paste and mix to fully combine. - 3 cups spinach

Turn the mixture out onto a clean, workable surface and knead until a soft, smooth, dough ball forms. This should take about 5-10 minutes. It should be soft and springy to the touch. - For the Spinach Noodles
Wrap in plastic wrap and rest for about 15 minutes. - For the Spinach Noodles
Roll out the dough to about ⅛ inch thick. - For the Spinach Noodles
Using a pasta machine on the fettucine setting or a paring knife, cut and transfer the uncooked pasta to a parchment-lined baking sheet along with a dusting of flour.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add salt. Add noodles and cook for only about 2 minutes, or until tender. Drain noodles and rinse in cold water. - 1 tsp salt - For the Spinach Noodles
Add cooked noodles to a serving bowl. Ladle warm fish stock over the top and serve immediately. - For the Spinach Noodles - For the Fish Stock
